_comment: Defects in the LOCKED v1 instrument that are known, recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed in place.
A locked instrument cannot be edited after the data are seen; that is what 'locked' means, and
editing it would make every number produced under it unattributable to any document. So a defect
found after the lock has exactly two honest destinations: this file, and the next version.
check_instrument.R fails the build on ANY instrument self-contradiction that is not listed here.
An entry here is not an excuse. It is a debt, with the finding that measured it and the version
that pays it off. When rubric v2 is locked, the entry is DELETED and the check enforces silently.

defects.found_by: an Opus screening agent, in one clause of a report about something else; independently repeated by a second agent
defects.summary: protocol/rubric.md and protocol/screening-schema.json name two different controlled vocabularies for `genre`. They overlap on 2 values out of 11. Every screener was handed both and told to obey both.
defects.consequence: The genre field of the v1 screen is UNUSABLE. It is reported (finding 24) and used for nothing downstream. It is NOT remapped: harmonising the arms after seeing how they diverged would destroy the only evidence that they did.
defects.why_not_fixed_in_place: v1 is the instrument 5,000 works were screened against. Editing it now would silently re-describe work already done under the old text.
defects.paid_off_in: rubric v2, seam 11: one vocabulary, in one place, machine-checked against the schema before any model runs
